provenance.title: Quantum Cryptanalysis on IBM Quantum Hardware: Extending Even-Mansour Period Recovery from N=4 to N=10
provenance.abstract: Genuine, un-compiled, textbook-faithful quantum cryptanalysis of symmetric-cipher structures on real IBM hardware (ibm_kingston, Heron generation). Using Simon's algorithm, the hidden period of the Even-Mansour cipher is recovered up to security parameter N=10 on real hardware (vs. a prior N=4 record), and periods of a 3-round Feistel (DES-family) construction are recovered at block sizes 6 and 8. A breadth-first benchmark of five genuine quantum attacks spans four symmetric-cipher paradigms ...
key_claims: Real-hardware Even-Mansour period recovery extended from a prior record of N=4 to N=10 (clean/rank-1 up to N=5; quantum-narrowing + classical-verification hybrid for N=6-10).
Clean (rank-1) recovery of 3-round Feistel (DES-family) hidden periods at block sizes 6 and 8 on real hardware, each validated against an independent control key.
Single-query Bernstein-Vazirani extraction of a 16-bit linear secret on real hardware.

A breadth-first benchmark of 5 genuine (un-compiled) quantum attacks across 4 symmetric-cipher paradigms (linear/BV, unstructured search/Grover, hidden-period/Simon), validated in statevector simulation to a 25-qubit classical ceiling.

Explicit scope disclaimer: attacks follow the birthday bound (no quantum advantage over classical collision-finding), target reduced/structured constructions (not full AES-256/RSA-2048/16-round DES), and rely on error mitigation rather than fault-tolerant error correction.

architecture.primary_variant: Simon's-algorithm hidden-period recovery applied to the Even-Mansour cipher (N up to 10, real hardware), combining a clean/rank-1 regime (N<=5) with a quantum-narrowing + classical-verification hybrid regime (N=6-10).

modules.name: bv_oracle_and_circuit
modules.output_shape: n-bit classical secret string a, extracted in a single query
modules.notes: Textbook Bernstein-Vazirani oracle + Hadamard-transform readout; explicit and standard.

modules.name: grover_spn_oracle_and_circuit
modules.output_shape: recovered SPN key after ~ (pi/4)*sqrt(2^n) Grover iterations
modules.notes: Iteration-count formula and target sizes are explicit, but the reduced SPN construction itself (S-box, round count, key schedule) is never spelled out -- only referred to generically as 'a reduced SPN construction' with a known plaintext/ciphertext pair. SIR ambiguities[3].

modules.name: simon_even_mansour_oracle_and_circuit
modules.input_shape: n-qubit register (n=5..10; qubit counts 15,18,21,24,27,30 per Table 1)
modules.output_shape: hidden period s=k1 (clean at n<=5) or ranked candidate list with true-key rank tracking the birthday bound 2^(n/2) (n=6..10, hybrid)
modules.notes: The clean/differential-Simon regime at n<=5 is standard Simon's algorithm and well specified. The n=6..10 'hybrid top-K + classical verification' regime, however, is the paper's central real-hardware contribution, and its exact mechanism -- how top-K candidates are formed from noisy measurement counts, and what the 'classical verification over the shortlist' step computes -- is described narratively, not algorithmically. Critically, the paper explicitly states that the specific 'hardware-aware circuit-conditioning and readout post-selection technique' that enables this is WITHHELD pending an IP decision (Section 5, S4) -- see SIR ambiguities[0], the single most consequential gap in this SIR.

modules.name: simon_cbcmac_forgery_oracle_and_circuit
modules.output_shape: hidden period s = Ek(a) XOR Ek(b), enabling existential forgery

parameters.construction: f(x) = Ek(x XOR c.a) XOR Ek(x XOR c.b)

modules.notes: Explicit oracle formula and hidden period; simulation-only (not run on real hardware).

modules.name: simon_feistel_oracle_and_circuit
modules.input_shape: 1+4m qubits for block size 2m (block 6 -> 13 qubits, block 8 -> 17 qubits, block 10 -> 21 qubits)
modules.output_shape: hidden period s=(1,gamma), gamma=F1(alpha0) XOR F1(alpha1); rank-1/clean if F2 is a permutation

parameters.construction: f(b,x) = LeftHalf(E(x,alpha_b)) XOR alpha_b = F2(x XOR F1(alpha_b))
parameters.block_10_status: verified in simulation, submitted to hardware (queued at submission time)

modules.notes: Explicit construction and qubit-count formula. Paper stresses that placing the variable on the left (x) and the constant on the right (alpha_b) is essential -- reversing this admits no hidden period; this constraint is called out clearly and is easy to preserve in code.

modules.name: readout_error_mitigation_stack
modules.output_shape: mitigated measurement distribution used for period/candidate extraction
modules.notes: The general mitigation stack (readout calibration, dynamical decoupling, twirling) is named and cited to a specific published method (Nation et al.), but the paper states the precise technical specifications 'are documented in Supplementary Table S1' -- which, in the provided document, shows only literal '[measurement]' placeholders in the Shots column (Table 4) rather than actual values. See SIR ambiguities[1].

modules.name: withheld_hardware_scaling_technique
modules.notes: The paper explicitly states: 'Achieving clean period recovery at the reported noise levels and structure sizes additionally relies on a hardware-aware circuit-conditioning and readout post-selection technique. The full specification of that technique is withheld in this draft pending an intellectual-property decision.' This module CANNOT be reproduced from the paper text. It is included here as an explicit placeholder so downstream stages do not silently invent a substitute without flagging it. See SIR ambiguities[0] (Critical).

modules.name: statevector_simulator_backend
modules.output_shape: exact statevector / measurement statistics for un-compiled circuits
modules.notes: Ceiling and example memory/time figures are explicit; exact simulator internals (e.g. which statevector library/kernel) are not detailed beyond 'QuantumOS on NVIDIA B200'.

datasets.name: Synthetic cipher instances (Even-Mansour, 3-round Feistel, CBC-MAC, reduced SPN) with randomly chosen target + independent control keys
datasets.split: per-instance; each cipher structure evaluated with a target key and a control key

metrics: rank of true key among ranked candidates (rank-1 = clean/exact recovery)
two-qubit gate fidelity (reported for block-8 Feistel: 219/233)
baselines: Koehler et al. (arXiv:2604.25509) -- prior largest reported real-hardware Even-Mansour recovery at N=4, cites a practical barrier at N=5 due to 'DORCIS tool limitations'
evaluation_protocol.compute: Real hardware: IBM ibm_kingston (Heron generation) via Qiskit. Simulation: 'QuantumOS' genuine statevector simulator on an NVIDIA B200 GPU, validated up to a 25-qubit classical-simulation ceiling (EM n=8 -> 24 qubits/0.27GB; Feistel block 12 -> 25 qubits/72s; block 14 -> 8.6GB wall; Simon n=16 would need ~4.5 PB, deemed infeasible).
special_conditions: Every cipher instance evaluated with two independent keys (target + control) to rule out coincidental/artifactual recovery
Readout error-mitigation stack applied to all real-hardware runs (readout calibration, dynamical decoupling, twirling; Nation et al. [12])
For Even-Mansour n=6..10: quantum-narrowing + classical-verification hybrid (top-K candidates, K=16,16,32,64,128), since true-key rank does not reach rank-1 beyond n=5
3-round Feistel block-10 (21 qubits) verified in simulation and submitted to real hardware but only 'queued' at submission time -- not a completed real-hardware result
Explicit non-claims: no quantum advantage (birthday-bound-limited), not full AES-256/RSA-2048/16-round DES, error mitigation (not fault-tolerant correction), Q2 oracle model assumed

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Because the paper's central real-hardware noise-scaling method (the 'hardware-aware circuit-conditioning and readout post-selection technique') is explicitly withheld, a faithful reproduction can only implement the STANDARD, publicly-documented Simon's-algorithm / BV / Grover circuits plus the published Nation et al. readout-mitigation stack. This will very likely reproduce clean recovery only up to the sizes the prior baseline (Koehler et al.) already achieved (~N=4-5), not the paper's claimed N=6-10 hybrid results, since the paper itself implies the standard stack alone is insufficient at those sizes.
implementation_assumptions.basis: explicitly stated in paper (Section 5, S4 'Disclosure of methods')
alternatives: Implement a best-effort, self-designed top-K/classical-verification heuristic as a stand-in, clearly labeled as NOT the paper's actual (withheld) method

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Per-job shot counts default to a standard Qiskit value (e.g. 4096 or 8192 shots) since Supplementary Table 4's 'Shots' column shows only '[measurement]' placeholders in the provided document rather than actual numbers.
alternatives: Sweep multiple shot counts and report sensitivity
Treat shot count as an unknown free parameter to be tuned for best rank recovery

implementation_assumptions.assumption: The reduced SPN construction targeted by the Grover attack is instantiated as a small, generic textbook SPN (e.g. a toy 3-4 round substitution-permutation network with a simple S-box) since the paper never specifies its S-box, round count, or key schedule.
alternatives: Use a miniature well-known toy cipher (e.g. a 'baby AES'/mini-SPN teaching construction) as a stand-in
Treat the SPN oracle as a black-box parameter the user must supply

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Real IBM hardware execution (ibm_kingston, Heron generation) requires an IBM Quantum account with backend access/credits, which cannot be assumed available in a reproduction environment; code defaults to Qiskit Aer (noiseless and/or noisy-simulator) backends, with an optional hook to swap in a real IBM backend if the user supplies credentials.
alternatives: Require the user to configure real hardware access before running anything

implementation_assumptions.assumption: The classical top-K candidate-narrowing + verification step for Even-Mansour n=6..10 is implemented as: take the K most frequent measurement bitstrings from the (mitigated) distribution, treat each as a candidate linear-system solution attempt, and rank candidates by how well they satisfy the collected Simon linear constraints, reporting the true key's position in that ranking -- since the paper describes this narratively rather than as a precise algorithm.
alternatives: Use a different scoring function for ranking (e.g. weighted by measurement count rather than constraint-satisfaction)
Treat this whole hybrid step as unimplementable without the withheld technique and report standard-Simon results only

ambiguities.description: The paper explicitly withholds the specific 'hardware-aware circuit-conditioning and readout post-selection technique' that it says is required to achieve clean period recovery at the reported noise levels and sizes ('pending an intellectual-property decision'). This technique underlies the paper's headline real-hardware claim (Even-Mansour to N=10) for n>5. Without it, the paper's own framing implies standard methods plateau around the prior N=4-5 baseline.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Reproduce only the standard, publicly-documented Simon/BV/Grover circuits and the cited (published) Nation et al. mitigation stack; do not attempt to reverse-engineer the withheld technique.
alternatives: Design and clearly label a best-effort substitute heuristic for the withheld step
Limit reproduction claims strictly to the clean/simulation-only results (BV, CBC-MAC, Grover, EM n<=5, Feistel block 6/8) and treat EM n=6-10 hybrid results as unreproducible pending disclosure

ambiguities.location: Supplementary Table 4 ('Shots' column) vs. main-text reference to 'Supplementary Table S1'
ambiguities.description: The main text (Section 3.2) states that 'per-job shot counts' are documented in Supplementary Table S1 alongside full experimental provenance. However, the provided document's Table 4 shows the literal placeholder text '[measurement]' in the Shots column for every row, rather than actual numeric values -- this data is not extractable from the given PDF.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Treat shot counts as unknown; default to a standard value (e.g. 4096/8192) for any reproduction attempt.
alternatives: Contact the authors or check for a separate supplementary file/repository that may contain the real Table S1
Sweep a range of plausible shot counts and report sensitivity of rank recovery

ambiguities.description: The 'quantum-narrowing + classical-verification hybrid' procedure is described narratively (take top-K quantum-ranked candidates, confirm the period by classical verification over the shortlist) but not given as a precise, step-by-step algorithm -- e.g. exactly how candidates are ranked from noisy measurement counts, and what 'classical verification' concretely computes over the shortlist, are left unspecified.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Rank candidates by how well each satisfies the collected Simon-style linear constraints (GF(2) system), as this is the most natural 'classical verification' reading.
alternatives: Rank purely by raw measurement frequency
Some combination of frequency and constraint-satisfaction, weighted in an unspecified way

ambiguities.location: Table 2, row 2 ('Grover / SPN block cipher (key search)')
ambiguities.description: Unlike the Feistel, CBC-MAC, and BV constructions -- each given an explicit oracle formula -- the reduced SPN construction targeted by the Grover attack is never defined (no S-box, round count, or key schedule given), only referred to generically as 'a reduced SPN construction' with 'a known plaintext/ciphertext pair'.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Instantiate a small generic/toy SPN construction (e.g. a miniature textbook SPN) as a stand-in for reproduction purposes.
alternatives: Request the exact SPN specification from the authors
Substitute a different well-known small-block cipher entirely and note the substitution

ambiguities.description: Several rows give full or partially-truncated IBM Quantum job IDs (e.g. 'd940hmkql68s73c9ptg0', 'd9450anu.../d9450b4q...') apparently intended to allow independent verification of the real-hardware runs, but other rows show only '—' with no ID at all, and the truncated ones cannot be resolved to complete, checkable identifiers from the paper text alone.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Treat job IDs as unverifiable provenance metadata for reproduction purposes; do not assume they can be used to pull down the original run data.
alternatives: Attempt to query IBM Quantum's job history API with the partial IDs to see if they resolve
Request complete job IDs directly from the authors
